then.text: How's the cap? Don't wash it in hot water. Don't wash it at all, if you can help it. Tweed improves with weather.
You saw off that buyer! Grand. Now watch. The crotal for the rust, the heather and whin for the flecks, warp and weft, shuttle and beater...
The loom clacks for a long while. When Úna stops, there is a bolt of tweed the colour of a Donegal hillside in October, flecked with gold and purple.
And a bit for you. A cap. Every person who ever walked these hills in the rain wore one of these, and every one of them was right.
That fashion buyer is still hovering. He won't leave until somebody beats him at something. Would you?
Crotal from Glenveagh and heather and whin from Nóra? You've done the rounds! Let me get these in the dye pot...
Oh no. Him. That buyer from Dublin has been in all week wanting to buy the bolt before it's even woven. He'll not leave till somebody beats him. Would you see to him?

else.text: You've the heather and whin, but I still need crotal from the lichen gatherer by Errigal.

then.text: Crotal from the lichen gatherer by Errigal, then heather and whin from Nóra in Gaoth Dobhair. Off you go, the loom's getting cold.

else.text: {greeting} I'm Úna. I weave tweed, the way my mother did, and hers. But I've no dyes left, and a big order coming in.
Would you gather some for me? Crotal lichen from the woman picking it by Errigal, in Glenveagh. Then heather and whin from Nóra, the weaver in Gaoth Dobhair.
Bring them back and I'll weave you something. Go raibh maith agat!

tw_assistant.text: Tweed jackets, caps, scarves, all of it. Donegal tweed's been sold from this town since the 1800s. Have a look, no pressure. A little pressure.

then.text: I'll be back next season. With a bigger chequebook. And better creatures.

else.text: I am buying that bolt for the spring collection in Milan, and I am not leaving without it. Unless you beat me. Which you won't.

then.text: Fine. The weaver keeps her tweed. I'll just have to buy the cap like everyone else.

else.text: Darling, this is the most gorgeous tweed. The flecks! The texture! I must have the whole bolt. When is it woven? Is it woven yet? Is it woven now?
